function.name: get_current_weather
function.description: Retrieve the current weather conditions for a specified location in either Celsius or Fahrenheit. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

location.description: The location for which to retrieve the weather, in the format of 'City, State', such as 'San Francisco, CA' or 'New York, NY'.

unit.description: The unit of measurement for the temperature.

function.name: search_local_docs
function.description: Searches the local knowledge base for documents that match the given natural language query and returns relevant document entries. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

query.description: The search query expressed in natural language, such as 'What are the symptoms of a cold?'.

limit.description: The maximum number of documents to return.

include_metadata.description: Determines whether to include metadata for the documents in the search results.

**First Studio Ghibli film to win the Japan Academy Film Prize for Picture of the Year** | Year | Award | Winning Film | |------|-------|--------------| | **1998** | Japan Academy Film Prize – Picture of the Year | **“Princess Mononoke”** (released 1997) | *“Princess Mononoke”* was the first Ghibli feature to receive the top honor at Japan’s national film awards, beating out other domestic contenders such as *“The Last Emperor”* (which won the award in 1990 but was a foreign production). --- ### How its box‑office success amplified Ghibli’s international profile | Domestic performance | International impact | |----------------------|----------------------| | • Grossed **¥12 billion** (~US$100 million) in Japan – the highest‑grossing Japanese film of 1997.
• Became the **second‑highest‑grossing** animated film in Japan after *“Dragon Ball Z”* at the time.
• Earned **US$200 million+ worldwide** (including North America, Europe, and Asia). | • The record‑breaking domestic receipts proved that Ghibli could generate blockbuster revenue, giving the studio leverage in negotiating overseas distribution rights.
• The film’s wide theatrical release in the United States (via distributors such as Buena Vista/Disney) introduced American audiences to Ghibli’s distinct storytelling style and high‑quality hand‑drawn animation.
• Positive critical reception abroad (e.g., *The New York Times*, *Variety*) and strong word‑of‑mouth helped build a cult following among Western cinephiles.
• The financial success funded subsequent projects (e.g., *“Spirited Away”*, *“Howl’s Moving Castle”*), allowing Ghibli to secure larger budgets and more ambitious marketing campaigns overseas.
• The film’s environmental themes resonated globally, positioning Ghibli as a socially conscious studio and attracting partnerships with international broadcasters and streaming platforms. | In short, *Princess Mononoke*’s domestic blockbuster status and worldwide earnings gave Studio Ghibli the credibility and capital needed to expand beyond Japan. The film’s success paved the way for future titles to reach global markets, cementing Ghibli’s reputation as a premier animation studio worldwide.
